On the 15th of this month, officers from the National Security Division of the police searched Tin Man Bookstore and The Bookshop Left Behind, arresting two people from Tin Man Bookstore and three from The Bookshop Left Behind. They are alleged to have violated Article 24 of the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, which criminalises "acts with seditious intent done with a seditious intention." National security officers seized books and other items from the two bookstores. It is understood that the book in question is "Only Red Flowers Bloom: Identity and Belonging in the Xi Jinping Era" (《唯紅花綻放：習近平時代的認同與歸屬》) by Feng Zheyun.

Tin Man Bookstore opened in 1976, founded by Wong Sheung-wai, who returned to Hong Kong after studying in Taiwan that year. It is a long-established second-floor bookstore in Hong Kong, occupying a shop of approximately 600 square feet, with ceiling-high bookshelves and tens of thousands of books in its collection. It specialises in literature, history and philosophy books, and also publishes and distributes books, some of which concern mainland politics—part of which are commonly known as mainland China "banned books".

In the 1990s, the book "The Private Life of Chairman Mao" (《毛澤東私人醫生回憶錄》) sold extremely well. According to an interview Wong Sheung-wai gave to Initium Media in 2016, Tin Man imported 300,000 copies of the book, with a net profit of HK$1.95 million from that single title. A review of records shows that the book was written by Li Zhisui, who served as Mao Zedong's personal physician from 1954 to 1976. The book records his observations of Mao in daily life, as well as insider accounts of the Chinese Communist Party's top leadership at the time. Tin Man Bookstore also published "The Truth About the Cultural Revolution Rebels" (《「文革」造反派真相》) by Zhou Lunzuo in 2006, and "The Cultural Revolution: Historical Truth and Collective Memory" (《文化大革命：歷史真相和集體記憶》) edited by Song Yongyi in 2007.

Tin Man Bookstore is the third local independent bookstore to announce its closure in recent months. Earlier this month, long-time Hong Kong Book Fair exhibitors Yulin Bookstore and Lok Man Bookstore were suddenly disqualified from participating by the Trade Development Council. Yulin Bookstore subsequently announced on social media on the 8th of this month that it would "gloriously end its storefront business" when its lease expires next April.

Less than a week after Yulin Bookstore announced its closure, The Bookshop Left Behind—founded in 2022 by veteran media practitioner Cen Yunhua and others—also announced on the 14th of this month that it would close on 30 August. At the time, The Bookshop Left Behind stated that an unpredictable "red line" was one of the reasons for its closure. One day after The Bookshop Left Behind announced its closure (the 15th), national security police carried out an arrest operation, raiding The Bookshop Left Behind and Tin Man Bookstore and arresting a total of five people. They are alleged to have violated Article 24 of the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, "acts with seditious intent done with a seditious intention." The case was referred to the police's National Security Division by the Customs and Excise Department, which stated that books with seditious intent had been discovered in a shipment of goods sent from outside Hong Kong. Following the incident, The Bookshop Left Behind did not open for business, and members of the public left notes of encouragement outside its door.
